text:
anya: Heads up — saw a reproducible latency oscillation on a subset of FIFO nodes during long-context streams. 95p went from 70ms -> 800ms for ~30s windows, then back.
liam: hmm, FIFO nodes only? did you check evicter logs or pager churn?
anya: yes, FIFO-only in the Canary pool. Evicter logs show repeated full-pass evictions and immediate reinserts. Pager activity spikes correspond.
maggie: can you paste a trimmed log snippet?
anya: sure:
```
2026-03-17T14:22:05Z evicter[pool=fifo-1] full_pass=true scanned=18000 evicted=14200 reinserts=13700 cpu_ms=120
2026-03-17T14:22:07Z pager[pool=fifo-1] page_in=14000 page_out=13980 latency_ms=312
2026-03-17T14:22:09Z evicter[pool=fifo-1] scanned=17500 evicted=0 reinserts=13450 cpu_ms=98
```
anya: note the reinserts count is almost as big as evicted — suggests reuses happening right after eviction.
devin: that sounds like eviction oscillation: items evicted then immediately needed by long contexts -> reinsert -> thrash. Any difference in LRU nodes?
anya: LRU nodes in same pool do not show the same amplitude. LRU has smoother tail latencies.
nikhil: interesting — could be FIFO's reinsert ordering interacting with async KV pager lock ordering. I remember a similar issue where eviction batches weren't atomic, so reinserts and concurrent readers competed and caused pager churn.
liam: can we repro locally with stress tool? use stress-kv --mode=long-context --warmup=30s --concurrency=64 --prefix-zipf=0.8
anya: repro steps: run that against a single FIFO replica, tail evicter logs, then run a steady 1 req/s long-context chat from a client to keep KV entries hot. reproduces reliably in ~2 minutes.
perf-bot: perf sample (CPU) attached: top stack: evicter::scan_loop -> memory::free_batch -> pager::async_page_out -> lock::wait
maggie: ok that's a lock stall path. If free_batch holds global slab lock while issuing async page outs, concurrent reinserts may block on slab and queue up — bursts when page_out completes -> reinserts rush -> another eviction.
devin: mitigation ideas: 1) make eviction batch atomically mark entries as "evicted" before page-out, so reinserts skip. 2) add a small hysteresis (dont-evict window) for items that were touched in last N ms. 3) tune batch size and add randomized jitter to avoid synchronized passes.
nikhil: also test switching FIFO -> approximate-LRU hybrid (per-bucket LRU tokens) to reduce reinsert tail. But need perf/space tradeoffs.
liam: quick experiment results I ran: evicter_batch=512 -> still thrash; batch=2048 -> worse; batch=128 + jitter=50ms -> 60% reduction in 95p spikes.
anya: another observable: heap in FIFO nodes grows slowly during the oscillation period and only shrinks after ~90s, suggesting fragmentation from reinsert chain.
maggie: fragmentation + frequent page_out/page_in will increase CPU and iowait. check kernel reclaim counters and fragmentation stats.
liam: can someone run a profiler with jemalloc background threads off? We saw allocator background threads can interact badly with our pager.
nikhil: I'll run a targeted experiment tomorrow: (A) atomically-mark-evicted patch, (B) don't-evict-if-last-touch<200ms, (C) hybrid-FIFO. Will report perf runs.
devin: for short-term mitigation, ops-bot can we route long-context traffic away from FIFO canaries?
ops-bot: routing change queued: will migrate 30% of long-context routing off fifo-1 to lru-2 over next 5m :white_check_mark:
liam: and add an alert on evicter.reinserts_rate > 5k/min + pager.latency_p99 > 200ms so we detect early.
anya: thanks — putting logs and a capture script in /mnt/tmp/evict-repro-2129803000.tgz and a runbook note: 
```
# repro
stress-kv --mode=long-context --concurrency=64 --duration=10m --target=fifo-1
tail -F /var/log/evicter.log | grep evicter
watch -n 1 'cat /proc/vmstat | grep pg'
```
maggie: one more ask — if we implement atomic-mark, be careful about correctness: must avoid a window where mark prevents legitimate readers from re-creating a value. test with interleaved read+write patterns.
nikhil: noted. I'll include unit+property tests that simulate concurrent read/insert during eviction.
anya: great. leaving reproduction artifacts and a small flamegraph in the bucket. thanks all :thumbsup:
